summary: Reviewed the uncommitted slice-9 diff (9 files, +431/-25) for MCP/OAuth resource-server hardening. No actionable defects found. Rate limiting is correctly wired to all 9 tools via a shared fixed-window limiter keyed on user_id:client_id; the limit=0 footgun is unreachable because config validation enforces rate_limit_max >= 1 and rate_limit_window_secs >= 1 in all environments and requires MCP_RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=1 in production. Same-origin enforcement via with_allowed_origins([origin]) is correct, and provider-outage token errors are mapped to sanitized static strings. The legacy Gateway::handle_authorized_tool_call path is test-only and not a rate-limit gap.
verification_commands: Read rmcp 3.1.4 streamable_http_server/tower.rs origin/host validation semantics
Cross-checked identity.rs (user_id: i64), auth.rs token_error_params, gateway.rs, main.rs, error.rs/oauth.rs InvalidToken paths
follow_up: rate_limiter.rs check_at `_ =>` branch allows one call even when limit=0 (inserts (1, now)); currently unreachable because config validation enforces rate_limit_max >= 1, but a defensive guard or debug_assert would harden it.
rmcp 3.1.4 allowed-origin matching is lenient on the port (a_port.is_none() || a_port == o_port) and passes when the Origin header is absent; acceptable for the same-origin intent but worth noting.
JSON-RPC error code -2004 is outside the MCP-recommended -32000..-32099 server error range; consider a code in that range for rate-limit responses.
The rate limiter is in-memory and single-instance only; a multi-replica deployment would not share the window. Acceptable for the current single-process deployment but a constraint to document.
